claims.text: Preserving FCC/BCC interface coherence enhances the creep resistance of dual-phase high-entropy-alloy protective coatings under continuous loading.
Coherent FCC/BCC interfaces impede dislocation motion.
The starting material is a dual-phase FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy protective coating with baseline interphase characteristics.
A controlled heat treatment can preserve or enhance FCC/BCC interface coherency.
Dislocation-mediated creep is dominant under the proposed moderate-temperature sustained-loading conditions.
Coherent FCC/BCC interphase boundaries act as pinning sites for dislocations.
Enhanced interface coherency impedes dislocation glide under continuous stress.
Enhanced interface coherency impedes dislocation climb under continuous stress.
Impeded dislocation glide and climb reduce plastic deformation and slow the creep rate.
Interface-coherency-enhanced coatings will have a significantly lower creep rate than coatings with lower interface coherency under identical loading conditions.
The proposed mechanism applies at moderate temperatures and stresses where dislocation motion dominates deformation.
At higher temperatures or stresses, diffusion creep or grain-boundary sliding may become active.
Activation of diffusion creep or grain-boundary sliding may diminish the creep-resistance benefit of coherent FCC/BCC interfaces.
The magnitude of creep-rate improvement may depend on processing details and alloy composition.
Interface coherency can be assessed by TEM or EBSD.
